Hi Adele — great questions and thanks for the traffic sketch. Short answers up front, followed by a proposed pilot plan.

Short answers:
- Hosted sandbox: yes — we can provision a sandbox project with an endpoint mapping that mirrors production behavior. You get a unique API key, streaming enabled, and an IP allowlist for your testers.
- Rate/burst limits: baseline hosted endpoints enforce a per-api-key token/s request ceiling and a per-endpoint concurrency soft-limit. For numbers similar to your profile we'd expect to suggest a baseline of 300 rps burst with an enforced sustained token throughput cap; precise numbers depend on tokenization patterns.
- When to choose Dedicated: if you need strict throughput SLOs (predictable GPU-backed throughput at scale), data plane isolation, or single-tenant capacity guarantees (e.g., sustained multi-thousand rps or strict contractual SLA) then Dedicated is the right path. Hosted is often fine for most pilots and early production if you can accept transparent routing and shared capacity with network isolation controls.

Proposed pilot plan (30-day):
1) Sandbox provisioning (hosted): provide one sandbox API key, two endpoint flavors (low-latency stream for agent assist; higher-throughput batch endpoint for nightly re-rank).
2) Throttle mapping: we will set a per-endpoint soft cap that matches the traffic_profile.csv; propose initial caps at 200 concurrent sessions / endpoint and a 300 rps burst allowance. We can tune after 48 hours of traffic.
3) Prefetch/KV cache: enable prefix KV caching for common prompts — this will reduce token spend and latency for your support flows.
4) Security: show you our KMS integration and audit log samples; for full KMS control we can explore VPC/private deployment later but hosted supports envelope encryption + audit streaming.
5) Syncs: schedule a 30-min technical sync (engineering + security) in the next 3 business days to confirm network allowlists and tokenization assumptions.

Next steps I need from you: a short confirmation on the initial caps above and an engineer (or two) to join the technical sync. If that works I'll kick off the sandbox request and share sandbox endpoint URLs and a minimal test harness.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
